_comment: Cold-start fallback (Growth-Strategist-Engine.md §3). Hand-authored general best practice, used only when an org has too little history to compute anything. Every recommendation built from this is marked confidence: low, with copy saying so — the alternative is an empty panel or a fabricated number, and both are worse.

X.bestTimes: Weekday mornings in your audience's timezone tend to out-perform evenings for text posts; replies land better mid-afternoon.
X.contentTypes: Threads generally out-reach single posts when the first line stands alone. Quote-posts on something already moving beat cold takes.
practices: The first line decides whether anything else gets read — no throat-clearing.
One idea per tweet in a thread; a tweet that needs the next one to make sense loses people.
Two or three hashtags at most, and only where they read naturally.

TIKTOK.bestTimes: Near-daily posting outperforms bursty posting for new accounts; consistency matters more than the specific hour early on.
TIKTOK.contentTypes: Native-feeling footage beats polished ads. Duet/stitch formats borrow reach from something already working.
practices: Lead with the hook, not a logo intro — the first three seconds carry the whole post.
On-screen text is a core element, not an accessibility afterthought.
Match a trending sound by pace and mood, not just by popularity.

INSTAGRAM.bestTimes: Late morning and early evening on weekdays are the common peaks; Reels keep circulating for days, so timing matters less for them than for feed posts.
INSTAGRAM.contentTypes: Carousels are the explainer format and drive saves; Reels drive reach. Saves and shares matter more than likes.
practices: The cover slide decides whether anyone swipes — write it before the rest of the deck.

FACEBOOK.bestTimes: Weekday mid-mornings tend to see the most comment activity; groups are more forgiving of timing than pages.
FACEBOOK.contentTypes: Longer conversational posts outperform short broadcast ones. Native text beats link-outs, which suppress reach.
practices: End on an explicit question — the algorithm rewards comments specifically.
Groups are where the real engagement lives; the page is the storefront.
Put the substance in the post rather than behind a link.

YOUTUBE.bestTimes: Publishing a day or two ahead of when your audience watches gives the algorithm time to test the video; weekends skew towards longer sessions.
YOUTUBE.contentTypes: Long-form is retention-driven; Shorts are hook-driven and keyword-tagged for search. They serve different jobs.
practices: Design the title and thumbnail together — never generate them separately.
The cold open has to pay off the title within the first fifteen seconds.
Chapters help retention and give search something to index.
